metadata.page_title: RLSI-6059 searchEmployer SBS to support pagination

text:
What is the Problem / Opportunity
---------------------------------

The platform operator is enabling the Workplace Pension product which requires a large number of Employers to be stored in Sonata. Employers, Advisors and the platform operator will maintain the Employer data using external Web Journeys, hence it is required to enhance the Employer search API exposed by Sonata.

Due to a large number of Employers stored in the system, it is required to support pagination of the results returned by the Employer search to meet the performance requirements for Web journeys.

~~*"BRA-151053 - Cannot find a unique scheme location for id = null, name = null, number = null, short name = null, reference=  <value>, refCode=  <ext ref type>"*~~

~~However not all Employer External References are configured as unique which allows setting up the same External Reference value against multiple Employers and the SBS should be able to return all Employers which meet the search criteria.~~

~~The validation which verifies that only one Employer meets the search criteria where Employer External Reference is provided must be removed and returning multiple search results should be allowed as it is for other search criteria. Services **other than** searchEmployer which use this validation should not be impacted by this change and still return the error when a unique Employer cannot be identified.~~

~~Based on the current implementation of the searchEmployer service, returning multiple Employers with the same value of External Reference will be possible if the external reference passed in the request is equal to external reference type selected in *Employer Reference Template*. This means the Platform Operator will have to pre-configure the employer external reference type by which the searches are performed.~~

| Scheme | **searchEmployer** | SearchEmployerRequestType/  pagingRange/  dgt:PagingRangeType | Optional | Min: 0  Max: 1 |  | Request paging by passing first row and page size. | The Paging Range element will allow to return a subset of results which meet the specified search criteria.  The element allows to specify how many results should be returned per page and what is the index of the first row returned. It also returns the total number of results meeting the search criteria.  The element will be optional in the request and if not provided, the default value will be 20 results per page beginning with the result with index 1.  The results will be ordered by the Employer Number (sloc\_code). |
